name: Enzyme peel (papaya/pumpkin)

lead: An enzyme peel uses fruit enzymes such as papain from papaya to loosen dead skin cells, and is marketed as milder than acid peels.
A 2022 lab study found that only two of eleven commercial products had sufficient protease activity, and no human trials were found.

paras: Protease enzymes break protein bonds in surface skin cells, aiming for gentle exfoliation without acids.
Papain has been linked to allergic hypersensitivity reactions, and people with latex allergy may be at higher risk of reacting to papaya.

lead: An enzyme peel is a cosmetic exfoliant marketed as a gentler alternative to acid peels. It uses fruit-derived enzymes, most often papain from papaya or enzymes from pumpkin or pineapple, with the stated aim of loosening dead surface skin cells.

Papain is a cysteine protease that breaks peptide bonds and is obtained from papaya latex [1]. A 2022 laboratory study of eleven commercial products advertised as enzymatic found that only two showed sufficient protease activity against casein, a generic protein substrate [2]. No human clinical trial of enzyme peels was identified for this article.

paras: Enzyme peels are applied as masks and rinsed off. Chemical peel references describe acid-based categories, alpha hydroxy acid and beta hydroxy acid peels, as the mildest peel types, with stinging, redness and dryness as expected light effects [3]. Enzyme peels are not discussed in that reference.

In a laboratory comparison, pineapple flesh showed the highest specific protease activity, and only two of eleven commercial enzyme peels had sufficient activity against casein; the authors compared products with pineapple and papaya fruit [2]. This tested enzyme activity, not effects on human skin.

In 2008 the US FDA moved to stop marketing unapproved topical papain drug products after reports of allergic hypersensitivity reactions, and people with latex allergy may be at higher risk of reacting to papaya [1]. Cosmetic enzyme peels are a separate product category from those drug products.
No studies found. A 2022 laboratory study measured the enzyme activity of commercial peels but did not test skin outcomes [2].

timeline.event: FDA acts against unapproved topical papain drug products after allergic reaction reports [1].
Laboratory study tests protease activity of eleven commercial enzyme peels [2].
